judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Content Standards (same statement-type grain) under Strand 1: Number / Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations, so hierarchy and rank are equal (rank 2 both) and cannot alone set direction. The statement texts give substantive pair-specific evidence: B6.1.2.1 (second) covers mental mathematics strategies and number properties to determine answers for basic multiplication facts to 144 and related division facts, while B6.1.2.2 (first) requires understanding of multiplication of a 2- or 3-digit number by a 2- or 3-digit number. Fluency and strategic use of basic multiplication facts and number properties (e.g. distributive/associative reasoning) directly supports success with multi-digit multiplication, which is a broadening to larger numbers and combined partial products. There is genuine conceptual coherence — percentages are a decimal/part-of-a-whole representation and finding a percentage of a quantity is commonly carried out as a decimal-by-whole-number multiplication — so the two reinforce each other meaningfully. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment; note that both endpoints carry unresolved ancestry and truncated source evidence, so hierarchy was not used as positive placement evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Content Standards (same statement grain, same coordinate rank 0) but sit in different strands: B4.4.1.2 is Strand 4 Data / Data Collection, Organization, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis (construct and interpret pictographs and bar graphs involving many-to-one correspondence to draw conclusions), while B4.1.2.1 is Strand 1 Number / Number Operations (recall basic multiplication facts up to 12 x 12). There is genuine conceptual coherence: many-to-one correspondence in scaled pictographs/bar graphs is inherently multiplicative, so multiplication-fact fluency is a natural complement when reading and constructing scaled graphs. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 4 Indicators (rank 0, same grade coordinate) concerned with mathematical patterning: B4.1.1.3.5 'Generate and analyse patterns in square numbers' (Strand 1 Number, Sub-strand Counting, Representation & Cardinality) and B4.2.1.3.2 'Identify and extend the patterns in a table or chart to solve a given problem' (Strand 2 Algebra, Sub-strand Patterns and Relationships). Their Learning Components confirm shared pattern-recognition/extension skill ('generate/analyse patterns in square numbers' vs 'identify/extend the patterns in a table or chart'), so there is substantive conceptual coherence: analysing a numeric pattern such as square numbers reinforces, and is reinforced by, identifying and extending patterns organised in tables or charts. However, the two sit in different strands with different content standards (understanding factors, multiples and squared numbers vs representing/extending patterns using charts and tables to solve problems), and at the same BASIC 4 rank there is no pair-specific evidence that proficiency in one is developmentally required for or clearly precedes success in the other; the tabular problem-solving context is a different application rather than a deepening of square-number patterning. Complementary reinforcement without a justified developmental direction supports symmetric relatesTo. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge/code context.
